title: AuthorQueryResult
description:
`author.query` result: one row per match over the staged world, each carrying
its support, grade, standing, and (when asked) its why-antichain.

root_hash.description:
The workspace digest the query was evaluated against (`jcs:sha256:`
regime — the staged world is workspace state, not a store commit).
0.6.0 only.

rows.description: The answer rows over the staged world.

valuation.description:
The full effective valuation of the staged world — every ruled atom
with its boolean, sorted by name. 0.6.0 only.

Grade.description:
How strongly a claim is known, weakest to strongest.

The derived `Ord` is the semantics: `Asserted < Attested < Tested <
Checked`. A claim's grade can only rise as evidence accumulates.

The grade axis measures the *recheckability of the establishing procedure*,
not the authority of the speaker (`docs/spec/07-verdicts-and-llm-boundary.md`
§1). `Asserted` is the strongest word and the weakest evidence: authorial
fiat grades below a model's opinion because there is nothing to re-run — not
because the author is outranked. Authority lives in the valuation layer; the
lattice ranks evidence, the ledger ranks authority (charter koan 6).

oneOf.description: Grounded in will; there is nothing to re-run — author's word.
A stored model judgment: re-posable and contestable, not re-derivable.
Re-derives statistically — a battery over a committed spec and seed.
Re-derives exactly — anyone re-runs it and gets the same result.

QueryRow.description:
One answer row: the matched ground atom, its variable bindings, the verdict
(support and grade) for that binding, and the atom's status under the
valuation the query was evaluated in.

atom.description: The matched ground atom, rendered `pred(a, b)`.

status.description: The atom's standing under the ambient valuation.

verdict.description: The support and grade for this binding.

why.description:
The support antichain rendered for a reader, present only when the query
asked for it ([`QueryOpts::why`]). Absent otherwise, so a plain query's
wire form is unchanged.

Status.description: A claim's three-valued standing under `(ν, Θ)`, derived — never stored.

oneOf.description:
Every monomial is `Θ`-unsatisfiable: the claim holds in no admissible
world. (Whether this is rejection or mere supersession is a `C`
question, outside the algebra.)

Some monomial is `Θ`-satisfiable but none is resolved-and-undefeated: the
shadow layer.

Some monomial holds on resolved events alone, with that monomial's own
defeater not fully ruled: assertable.

ValuationEntry.description:
One ruled event variable in a wire valuation: the atom's resolved name and
the boolean it was ruled to. Explicit-false rulings are semantically
distinct from unruled atoms (a false kills a monomial; unruled leaves it
possible), so the wire form carries both — never a true-only list.

Verdict.description:
The outcome of asking about a claim, carried over two orthogonal channels
that never entangle (`docs/spec/07-verdicts-and-llm-boundary.md` §1):

- **support** — the positive-boolean formula over citations and assumptions:
  *what the conclusion rests on* (`02-semantics.md`).
- **grade** — *how the procedure stacked on that ground was verified.*

The channels are independent: a conclusion may rest on weak-authority
citations in the support channel and still be `checked` in the grade
channel, because grade rolls up over the procedure chain and never descends
into the citations. See [`Verdict::of_procedure`] for the worked answer to
the collapse worry.

grade.description: Channel two: the strength of the establishing procedure.

support.description: Channel one: the hypotheses under which the claim holds.

Why.description:
The positive explanation of an atom: its support antichain rendered for a
reader.

The [`antichain`](Why::antichain) is the disjunction of minimal witnesses —
the same shape as [`crate::SupportIndex::why`], one inner vector of
[`ClaimId`]s per minimal monomial of the support (sign is dropped, matching
that seam). [`rendered`](Why::rendered) is the parallel human line for each
witness, resolved to claim names through the world's interner; a negative
literal renders with a `not ` prefix, and the unconditional witness (the
empty monomial) renders as `unconditional`.

antichain.description: The disjunction of minimal witnesses, each a conjunction of claim ids.

rendered.description: The per-witness human rendering, index-aligned with `antichain`.
